image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a European fire salamander's head and upper torso amidst green grass. The subject features glossy black skin with distinct yellow markings above the eyes and on the snout. Blades of grass partially obscure the lower jaw and foreground.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape appears somewhat rounded rather than distinctly broad/flattened in this angle. Crucially, the prominent parotoid glands behind the eyes are not clearly visible or defined; the area blends into the neck without the characteristic swelling.

Only the head and very front of the shoulders are visible; the full body cylinder cannot be verified due to framing.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The yellow patches have a slightly 'painted-on' or airbrushed quality, lacking the subtle integration with the skin pores/texture seen in the black areas. They look like flat overlays.
The mouth line is indistinct and seems to merge with the snout. There is no clear definition of the jaw hinge or mouth opening, giving the face a slightly melted or featureless lower region.
The foreground grass exhibits a smudged, plastic-like blur rather than optical depth-of-field bokeh, suggesting generation artifacts in fine linear details.
